## Overview

Objects generated by `letsR`, including `PresenceAbsence` objects and
the outputs of functions such as `lets.envpam` and `lets.attrpam`,
may contain spatial rasters stored as `SpatRaster` objects from the
`terra` package. Because these objects may reference external data
or memory resources, saving them directly with the base R `save()`
function may not preserve their contents correctly.

To ensure reliable serialization, `letsR` provides two functions:
`lets.save()` and `lets.load()`. These functions work similarly to
the base R `save()` and `load()` functions, but automatically handle
spatial raster components. All `SpatRaster` elements are prepared
for serialization when saving and reconstructed when loading,
preserving the original object structure.

## Saving and loading objects

The same workflow can be applied to different types of `letsR`
objects. For example, a `PresenceAbsence` object can be saved
and subsequently restored as follows:

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(letsR)

# Load example data
data(PAM)

# Save the PresenceAbsence object
lets.save(PAM, file = "PAM.RData")

# Load the saved object
PAM <- lets.load(file = "PAM.RData")
```

The functions also support objects returned by `lets.envpam()`
and `lets.attrpam()`, without requiring any additional arguments
or modifications.

```{r examples}
# Save and load an environmental PAM object
lets.save(envpam, file = "envPAM.RData")
envpam <- lets.load("envPAM.RData")

# Save and load an attribute PAM object
lets.save(pam_att, file = "attrPAM.RData")
pam_att <- lets.load("attrPAM.RData")
```

In all cases, matrix components, spatial rasters, and other object
attributes are preserved, allowing the restored objects to be
used directly in subsequent analyses.
